subject: Archaeology
title: The Lascaux Cave Paintings
description: Learn The Lascaux Cave Paintings in one minute.

hook.text: Four teenagers chasing a dog into a hole in 1940 discovered the most spectacular cave paintings in the world.

buildup.text: Lascaux's walls are covered with over 600 paintings of horses, bulls, deer, and one mysterious bird-headed man.

discovery.text: The paintings are 17,000 years old. Artists used mineral pigments blown through bone tubes for shading and texture.

twist.text: Tourist breath caused mold to attack the paintings. Lascaux was sealed in 1963.

climax.text: No one knows why they were painted. Hunting magic, storytelling, or spiritual rituals — all theories remain unproven.

punchline.text: Teenagers found the Sistine Chapel of the Ice Age. Now no one is allowed inside.

quiz.question: Why was Lascaux Cave sealed to the public in 1963?
options: The French government wanted to charge higher admission fees
Tourist breath caused mold that was damaging the paintings
Vandals scratched their names into several of the panels

details.summary: The Lascaux cave in France contains stunning paintings of animals created around 17,000 years ago. Over 600 figures of horses, bulls, deer, and abstract symbols fill its walls, representing one of the greatest artistic achievements of the Upper Paleolithic period.
details.whyItMatters: Lascaux proves that Ice Age humans were sophisticated artists with aesthetic sensibility. The cave challenges any assumption that art is a modern invention and shows that creativity is deeply embedded in human nature.
takeaways: Lascaux contains over 600 painted figures from 17,000 years ago
Animals include horses, aurochs, deer, and abstract symbols
The cave demonstrates sophisticated Upper Paleolithic artistry

faq.question: Why were the Lascaux paintings made?
faq.answer: Their purpose is debated. Theories include hunting magic, shamanistic ritual, seasonal calendars, and social gathering spaces. The location deep inside caves, beyond natural light, suggests the paintings had ritual or spiritual significance rather than purely decorative purposes.

faq.question: Can visitors still see the original Lascaux paintings?
faq.answer: No. The cave was closed in 1963 because breath moisture and CO2 from visitors were damaging the paintings. A precise replica called Lascaux IV now allows visitors to experience the art without harming the originals, which are monitored constantly.
